records.subject: Saint Bartholomew, apostle; martyrdom
records.title: The Martyrdom of Saint Bartholomew
records.rights: Object page expressly states image is free/public domain; NGA Open Access policy
records.composition: Near-square, dramatic chiaroscuro; martyrdom is depicted before the flaying. Original is distinct from previously APPROVED_LOCKED W02-001 Ribera Saint Bartholomew Apostolado portrait, not a substitute.
records.summaryEn: Ribera's dramatic 1634 canvas depicts the Apostle Bartholomew facing martyrdom, with the executioner's blade in the foreground. It is a distinct physical work from the previously approved Ribera apostle portrait.
records.summaryFr: Cette toile dramatique de Ribera, datée de 1634, représente l'apôtre Barthélemy avant son martyre, le couteau du bourreau au premier plan. Il s'agit d'une œuvre distincte du portrait d'apôtre de Ribera déjà approuvé.

records.subject: Saint James the Greater, apostle; legendary miracles
records.title: The Miracles of Saint James the Greater
records.imageRoute: Museum object-page Download control; exact raw URL and dimensions not independently captured
records.rights: CMA object page explicitly permits copying, modification and distribution without permission
records.composition: Portrait composition; foreground Hermogenes and separate healing narrative. Legends rather than Gospel episodes; do not present as documentary apostolic history.
records.summaryEn: Coypel combines two traditional miracles attributed to Saint James the Greater: the conversion of Hermogenes and the healing of a paralytic. These are hagiographical traditions, not scenes recorded in the canonical Gospels.
records.summaryFr: Coypel réunit deux miracles traditionnellement attribués à saint Jacques le Majeur : la conversion d'Hermogène et la guérison d'un paralytique. Ce sont des traditions hagiographiques, non des épisodes rapportés dans les Évangiles canoniques.

records.subject: Saint Thomas, apostle; post-Resurrection encounter
records.title: The Incredulity of Thomas
records.imageRoute: Museum object-page Download image control; direct binary endpoint not captured
records.rights: Object-specific Public domain marking confirmed; Rijksmuseum policy permits reuse of public-domain/CC0 images
records.composition: Landscape Caravaggesque composition; Saint Thomas touches Christ's side. Museum states painter's Catholic/Protestant affiliation is not established; do not assert it.
records.summaryEn: Ter Brugghen portrays the risen Christ inviting Thomas to examine the wound in his side, a direct illustration of John 20:24–29. The artist's personal confessional affiliation remains undocumented.
records.summaryFr: Ter Brugghen représente le Christ ressuscité invitant Thomas à examiner la plaie de son côté, selon Jean 20, 24-29. L'appartenance confessionnelle personnelle du peintre demeure non établie.

records.subject: Saint Cecilia with an angel
records.artist: Orazio Gentileschi and Giovanni Lanfranco (museum's dual attribution)
records.title: Saint Cecilia and an Angel
records.rights: NGA object-specific public domain image and Open Access policy
records.composition: Horizontal chiaroscuro organ-and-angel scene. Museum documents historical collaborative attribution; not a sole-Gentileschi or sole-Lanfranco painting. May be difficult to crop without losing organ or angel.
records.summaryEn: Saint Cecilia plays a small organ while an angel holds music beside her. The National Gallery identifies the painting with both Orazio Gentileschi and Giovanni Lanfranco; its landscape arrangement needs deliberate mobile review.
records.summaryFr: Sainte Cécile joue d'un petit orgue tandis qu'un ange tient une partition. La National Gallery attribue l'œuvre à Orazio Gentileschi et Giovanni Lanfranco ; sa composition horizontale nécessite un contrôle particulier sur mobile.

records.subject: Saint Catherine of Alexandria; mystical marriage dream
records.title: The Dream of Saint Catherine of Alexandria
records.rights: NGA object-specific public domain image and Open Access policy
records.composition: Portrait-format Baroque devotional scene; a legendary dream, not an historical portrait. Do not conflate with approved All Souls Ludovico Carracci Purgatory painting.
records.summaryEn: Lodovico Carracci depicts Saint Catherine asleep as the Virgin and Child appear in her legendary mystical-marriage vision. The painting is a separate physical original from the user's approved Carracci work for All Souls.
records.summaryFr: Lodovico Carracci représente sainte Catherine endormie, visitée par la Vierge et l'Enfant dans la vision légendaire de ses noces mystiques. Cette œuvre est distincte du Carracci approuvé pour la Commémoration des fidèles défunts.

records.subject: Saint Nicholas of Myra/Bari, not Nicholas of Tolentino
records.title: Saint Nicholas of Bari
records.medium: tempera and gold leaf on wood panel
records.imageRoute: Museum object-page Download control; exact raw URL not captured
records.composition: Extremely narrow gold-ground full-length bishop portrait; differs from existing acquired Met Pietro di Giovanni d'Ambrogio Saint Nicholas, accession 459258. User's dark Baroque preference makes this an alternative only.
records.summaryEn: Crivelli depicts Saint Nicholas of Myra, venerated at Bari, in episcopal vestments with a crozier and three gold balls. This 1472 panel is a distinct object from the already archived Metropolitan Museum Saint Nicholas.
records.summaryFr: Crivelli représente saint Nicolas de Myre, vénéré à Bari, en vêtements épiscopaux, avec sa crosse et trois boules d'or. Ce panneau de 1472 est distinct du saint Nicolas du Metropolitan Museum déjà archivé.

records.subject: Saint Barbara
records.title: Saint Barbara
records.rights: NGA object-specific public domain and Open Access policy
records.composition: Part of a four-panel altarpiece; official download visibly includes architectural frame, which violates user's frame-free preference. Do not certify or auto-crop the physical panel.
records.summaryEn: The Saint Barbara panel belongs to a Portuguese late-medieval ensemble. Although the National Gallery provides a public-domain image, its current reproduction includes the elaborate frame and is not a frame-free hero master.
records.summaryFr: Ce panneau de sainte Barbe appartient à un ensemble portugais de la fin du Moyen Âge. Bien que l'image soit libre de droits selon la National Gallery, la reproduction actuelle comprend son encadrement et ne constitue pas un visuel principal sans cadre.

records.subject: Saint Margaret of Antioch, not Margaret of Cortona
records.title: Martyrdom of Saint Margaret
records.rights: NGA object-specific public domain image and Open Access policy
records.composition: Portrait martyrdom with dragon and sword; Margaret of Antioch iconography, not Saint Margaret of Cortona. Exact 1962 observance/rank and relevance need liturgical crosswalk before use.
records.summaryEn: Giuseppe Cesari's early-seventeenth-century panel shows the martyrdom of Saint Margaret of Antioch, identifiable by the dragon and executioner. It must not be confused with Saint Margaret of Cortona.
records.summaryFr: Ce panneau du début du XVIIe siècle de Giuseppe Cesari représente le martyre de sainte Marguerite d'Antioche, reconnaissable au dragon et au bourreau. Il ne faut pas la confondre avec sainte Marguerite de Cortone.

records.subject: Saint Lucy: two existing acquired NGA originals
records.evidence: platform/885-sacred-art-candidates data/calendar/sacred-art-candidates.v1.json already lists both as ACQUIRED_REVIEW_ARCHIVE_ONLY with hashes and original sizes; 451-work intake has both. Historical hashes not recomputed here.
records.summaryEn: Two direct Saint Lucy paintings already have source-verified image acquisition records. This pass prevents them being recounted as new artwork discoveries or new downloads.
records.summaryFr: Deux peintures représentant directement sainte Lucie disposent déjà de traces d'acquisition d'images vérifiées à la source. Elles ne doivent pas être comptées à nouveau comme découvertes ou téléchargements.
